On 26 July 2024, the Casper Network disclosed an elevation-of-privilege exploit that bypassed uref access-rights checks during contract installation, enabling unauthorized transfers from 13 wallets with reported losses of about $6.7 million. Some hack catalogues indexed the incident under “Solrise Finance,” although the public disclosure described a broader Casper Network vulnerability rather than a Solrise-specific contract flaw. Casper disclosed that attackers bypassed access-rights validation for uref resources during contract installation, allowing malicious contracts to gain unauthorized capabilities and perform token transfers.
